title: Man in Bigfoot costume prompts high number of calls to police in coastal Maine town - The Boston Globe
excerpt: In the end, Police Chief Erik Josephson wrote, a farce was the only thing that was afoot.
content:
Police in the tiny Maine coastal village of Damariscotta were inundated with calls on Tuesday reporting sightings of Bigfoot across town, officials said in a Wednesday social media post, addressing reports of a large and hairy individual roaming about town.

But in the end, Police Chief Erik Josephson wrote, a farce was the only thing that was afoot.

“Bigfoot is not real,” Josephson wrote in the post, a conclusion he said was only reached after a “lengthy, exhaustive, and completely serious investigation.”

He said that the department had received an usually high volume of calls reporting sightings of a yeti or Sasquatch like figure walking through town on Tuesday in the small village roughly an hour north of Portland.

Officer William Smith confronted the alleged creature on Main Street, Josephson said, and determined it was just a man wearing a “very convincing” Bigfoot costume.

The man was not identified, and Josephson said there was no evidence anything criminal had taken place. His motives remained unclear.

“Despite our best efforts to gather compelling evidence, not a single Bigfoot grunt was heard,” he wrote on social media, adding, “We understand this may be disappointing to some. Frankly, there were members of our department who were secretly hoping we had finally stumbled upon something that would make national news.”

Josephson said that police were charmed by the public’s investment in getting to the bottom of the Bigfoot mystery.

“While we didn’t find Bigfoot, we did find something almost as rare: a town full of people willing to stop what they’re doing to investigate a Bigfoot sighting and keep each other safe,” he said.
